First-Division Club Transfer Network
Which clubs act as hubs and bridges in LaLiga's transfer market, and how does the market split into trading communities?
Community (Louvain)
Group A — Atlético / Barcelona / Sevilla circuit
Group B — Alavés / Getafe / Betis circuit
Group C — Real Madrid / Athletic / Valencia circuit
Node type
LaLiga First-Division club (color = community)
Aggregated foreign league / Rest of the World
Node size & edges
Size ∝ weighted degree (players transferred in + out)
Line width ∝ number of players traded between two nodes
Technical Fact Sheet
Network name
LaLiga First-Division Transfer Network (2025–2027), filtered from the full UPY Transfer Market Project dataset.
Source
Fichajes.com (official transfer market tracker). Scraped and modeled in the UpyTransferMarketProject repository.
Filtering & methods (declared)
Only the 24 current First-Division clubs are kept; reserve/B teams (Alavés B, Real Madrid B, etc.) were removed. Foreign-league transfers stay aggregated exactly as provided (Premier League, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Rest of the World) — 5 macro-nodes. Metrics recomputed on this filtered graph with NetworkX; communities via Louvain.
Graph type
Undirected, weighted, simple graph (aggregated from a directed weighted multigraph of individual transfers). Connected — 1 component.
Centralities applied
Weighted degree (players moved in+out) · Betweenness (bridge role) · PageRank (influence via transfer flow)

2–3 findings (LaLiga clubs only, leagues excluded)
1Atlético de Madrid is the only club top‑3 in all three centralities (degree 42, betweenness 0.068, PageRank 0.044) — hub and bridge.
2Getafe has the highest weighted degree (47) despite linking to only 11 clubs — high-volume, concentrated trading.
3Celta de Vigo tops betweenness (0.070) though mid-table in degree — a quiet bridge between communities.
Tools
Python · BeautifulSoup4 · NetworkX · python‑louvain · Matplotlib · HTML/CSS
